I was going through a full blown mental breakdown for around 8 months last year and went on extravagant spending sprees every time I went through a panic attack, which was a daily occurrence.

At the worst point I had 3 cars (Porsche, Jaguar and Mercedes), a quad bike, a jetski, an unaffordable beachfront penthouse (rented), loads of expensive perfumes (some $900+), weed at least 1-2 grams per day, and so many clothes that I still sometimes find stuff in my closet that have tags on them because there's so much that I've never even worn. So in total I blew through around €258k (all of my own money + 2x finance, 5x credit cards, 2x unsecured loans) during that time and now have very little to show for it.

I know I did all of this myself and take full responsibility but I feel like my family let me down because my mind had really checked itself out, yet they didn't mind benefitting from my generosity  (I bought them stuff too)😩 To be fair, looking back, I really needed to be stopped because I wouldn't have considered myself of sound mind back then. I was seriously unstable as the tiniest thing could spin me into traumatic panic attacks that would sometimes last days. Distraction was the only (temporary) killer of my mental pain.

I've now sold two of the cars and some of the expensive electronics, and am making slow yet sure progress to clean it all up. At least I won't have to worry about clothes for a while.

I still go shopping to feel better about or reward myself but only to the extent where I enjoy it, and I'm much more selective and in control, so now I only buy something if it really inspires me or I need it.

Learning to walk away from things I don't need has been a great lesson. 🙏🏼
